title: Collective Partners tab: a Collective hub invites up to ten Spaces owned by other people, they opt in, and the tab shows the partner directory, what partners cross-list, and a shared calendar of it

source.ref: Owner spec 2026-10-16: "Collective is many owners working together; Network is one owner running many groups. The test is ownership." "A Partners tab on the hub Space. It lists invited partner Spaces, pending invites, and what each partner has cross-listed. There is a shared calendar of everything cross-listed and a partner directory page. There is no member list across partners, no chapter tree, and no control over another partner's Space." "A Space never shows both tabs. The plan decides which one renders." Build order: "Build the Collective Partners tab: cross-owner invites and the shared calendar on top of cross-listing."

detail: Migration 20270346009200 adds collective_partners (hub_space_id, partner_space_id, invited_by, responded_by, status pending/accepted/declined/revoked; service role only, like collective_cross_listings). A trigger enforces consent at commit: the hub is an active top-level Collective and its owner invites, the partner is an active visible Space owned by someone else, and only the partner owner accepts; an owner change on either Space revokes the consent. collective_listing_space_live is replaced (same signature) so an accepted partner of a live hub cross-lists like a member Space; cross-listing-store mirrors it through livePartnerSpaceIds. The cap is COLLECTIVE_PARTNER_CAP = 10 in lib/collective/partners.ts, enforced by the invite action, and pending invites count toward it. /spaces/<slug>/partners renders for Collective plans only: the partner directory, what each partner cross-listed inside the Collective, and a shared calendar of the public events of every cross-listed Circle and Journey (homed at the listing's source Space). The hub owner sees pending invites, the invite field (a Space handle or link) and End partnership. The profile nav shows Partners for collective and nonprofit_collective and Network for network, never both. The partner owner answers on settings/cross-listing, which gets its first menu door (space.listings under Reach). Not built: a notification for a new invite; /spaces/<slug>/network still resolves for existing Collectives by direct link, with no tab. The migration is not applied.
